text:
eli: Heads up — we just saw a huge spike in client retries to model-service in eu-west-1. 5xx rate up ~4x, but CPU on pods is low. Traffic counters show the same 3 endpoints taking ~85% of new connections.

marta: Whoa. Any infra events?

ops-bot: kube-proxy/daemonset rolling restart started at 2026-03-18T02:11:12Z on nodes: gpu-euw-1, gpu-euw-3, gpu-euw-5 (controlled rollout).

kevin: I pulled ipvs stats on the service VIP. Looks like destination <10.0.32.7:8080 has ~120k new conns while others are <15k.

marta: paste of what you ran?

kevin: `ipvsadm -Ln --stats` output (trimmed):
```
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP 10.96.130.22:8080 rr
  -> 10.0.32.7:8080                Masq    1      120482     42
  -> 10.0.32.9:8080                Masq    1       13210     11
  -> 10.0.34.2:8080                Masq    1       10933      7
```

eli: So ipvs is doing the routing, but why such skew? kube-proxy restarted during rollout. Could hash seed or conntrack state reset cause a transient regrouping?

sre-jen: Two hypotheses: 1) kube-proxy restart changed the consistent hash seed so existing long-lived connections got rehashed and new sync state caused blacklist/weighting mismatch. 2) Underlay MTU mismatch/fragmentation causing partial SYNs to be retried and ipvs mapping to a particular backend due to packet 5-tuple similarity.

oliver: We also see a small bump in RSTs on that dst pod in tcpdump: `tcpdump -n -i eth0 dst port 8080 and (tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-rst) != 0)` showed repeated SYN retransmits then RST from pod. Could be conntrack or kernel connlimit.

marta: Any RDMA/MTU differences between the nodes? We moved some gpu nodes to a different rack earlier this week and toggled jumbo frames on those NICs.

kevin: Good call — `ip -d link show` shows mtu 9000 on gpu-euw-3 but mtu 1500 on gpu-euw-5.

eli: That would cause fragmentation across path and might trigger retries. ipvs uses packet 5-tuple; if fragments cause retransmits they can get re-mapped oddly. Also kube-proxy restarts could have reset destination counters.

marta: Immediate mitigation: pin kube-proxy to previous image on the three restarted nodes and cordon gpu-euw-3 for rolling MTU fix. Also scale up model-service to absorb retries.

kevin: I rolled back kube-proxy on gpu-euw-3/5 and bumped `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` from 262144 -> 524288 on the affected hosts. Patch applied.

ops-bot: Triggered alert: `endpoint-traffic-skew` suppressed (silenced by @marta)

eli: After rollback and MTU normalization, traffic rebalanced across endpoints within ~7 minutes. Errors down to baseline.

oliver: Action items: add a pre-rollout check that validates NIC MTU across nodes in a kube-proxy rollout. Add an alert for >60% of new connections going to a single endpoint for 3m. Run a kube-proxy restart canary in staging that asserts no >2x endpoint skew.

marta: Also add a small diag script to capture `ipvsadm -Ln --stats`, `kubectl get endpoints -o wide`, `ip -d link`, and `ss -tn src :8080` into a single artifact when the skew alert fires.

eli: Thanks team — closing for now, will follow up with a short postmortem doc and RCA link. :thumbsup:
